title: Minimum One Bit Operations
description: Given a non-negative integer `n`, you may transform it into `0` using two operations any number of times: (1) change the rightmost bit (bit `0`), or (2) change bit `i` (`i > 0`) if bit `i - 1` is `1` and all bits from `0` through `i - 2` are `0`. Return the minimum number of operations needed to reduce `n` to `0`.
hints: The sequence of states visited when reducing `2^k` to `0` is the reflected binary Gray code, taking `2^(k + 1) - 1` steps.
The minimum steps from any `n` to `0` is the inverse Gray code of `n`, computed by repeatedly XORing `n` with `n >> 1` down to `0`.

examples.explanation: 0 is already zero, so 0 operations are needed.
